transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-06-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maria Gonzalez (Zenoria CTO), Priya Kapoor (Zenoria ML Eng), Tom Reynolds (Zenoria Infra), Eric Lee (Zenoria PM)

--- Auto Summary (may be imperfect) ---
Alex: Quick scoping to pick models and bench plan for 2-week POC, focus on accuracy for EN/ES, latency target ~<200ms p50 for 512-token responses, cost target TBD, security: VPC + KMS required.

00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about 42 minutes. quick intros?
00:10 Maria: Maria here, CTO, we want to validate open models for our multi-lingual support assistant, mainly english and spanish, and some domain-specific product faq answers.
00:20 Priya: hi i'm priya, i'll own the model evaluation and provide dataset examples.
00:25 Tom: tom - infra, will check VPC and network constraints.
00:28 Alex: great. Samir, could you frame success criteria?
00:34 Samir: sure, from redwood side typical success metrics we see: accuracy/answer quality (human-eval pass rate on benchmark prompt set), latency (p50/p95), token cost, and stability under parallelism. for this poc i'd propose: 1) quality threshold: 85% human pass on curated prompts, 2) latency p50 <200ms for 512 tokens on dedicated instance sim, p95 <600ms, 3) cost target — let's keep as discussion, but a ballpark so we can optimize quantization/batching.
01:05 Maria: that sounds reasonable. for us accuracy is king, especially spanish. if we trade a bit more latency for quality that's okay for initial test.
01:15 Alex: good, that'll influence model shortlist. quick question on usage: what's your expected qps and concurrency?
01:22 Eric: our prod plan: about 4–6 qps initially, spiky to 20 qps during peak, concurrency per request around 1–2, typical contexts 200–800 tokens.
01:35 Priya: plus occasional long context 4k tokens for conversation history, but most are short.
01:40 Samir: okay so bench should include a 512 token gen and a 4k context generation test. mixing short and long.
02:00 Alex: any strict data residency or retention limits?
02:05 Tom: we need VPC private deployment or at least private networking to our cloud, plus KMS for keys. SOC2 compliance is required.
02:12 Lena: Redwood Private supports VPC and KMS; for a PoC we can run in dedicated infra with private network peering. we'll include security docs. (link to deck: https://redwood.example.com/decks/zenoria-poc)
02:28 Maria: perfect. back to models, what are you thinking?
02:32 Samir: open-model shortlist for this profile: 1) Mistral Large/Instantiated variants (good perf/cost), 2) Llama 2 13B and 70B (70B for quality, 13B as cheaper baseline), 3) Falcon-40B-instruct, 4) Mixtral or Mistral 7B-instruct for faster cheap cases, 5) OpenAssistant/RedPajama family for multi-lingual checks. we'd also consider Llama3-like models if available downstream but for PoC we keep to widely-available open checkpoints.
03:10 Priya: for spanish quality which of these is best?
03:15 Samir: empirically 70B LLama2 variants and Mistral large tend to be solid; Falcon sometimes lags on esms... sorry i said 'esms' meaning spanish, transcription quirk, but bottom line: 70B and Mistral large are good candidates. Mixtral and 13B can be strong with instruction tuning for faq style.
03:35 Maria: cost of 70B will be high, we'd need to see quantized runs. what about 8-bit/4-bit quant?
03:42 Samir: yes quantization is key — we can run 4-bit quantized kernels. Redwood profiles will show throughput/latency for each quant profile. note that quality drop for aggressive quant might be slight but often acceptable for retrieval-augmented generation. we'll include top-line perf numbers in the shortlist doc.
04:05 Alex: also we should talk about fallback strategies — lower-cost smaller model for non-critical replies and heavy-weight for escalation.
04:12 Priya: yes, we need deterministic routing rules, maybe by confidence threshold.
04:18 Samir: Redwood can do smart routing based on cost/latency/quality rules, with automatic fallback to a smaller compatible variant if capacity is constrained. we'll demo that if needed.
04:32 Tom: on infra: for the POC we can open peering to a dedicated subnet; can you run benchmarks inside our VPC or do we need dedicated infra?
04:42 Lena: we can run in your VPC or Redwood Dedicated that peers to your VPC. for latency-on-the-wire we recommend running the bench inside your VPC so we measure real networking. for early quality tests we can run hosted bench runs.
05:00 Alex: ok let's capture bench plan: Samir?
05:05 Samir: plan: 1) synthetic latency runs (512 token, varying batch sizes), 2) quality eval (human-in-the-loop on 200 prompt set per language), 3) long-context stability (4k tokens) and memory/KV cache behavior, 4) concurrency stress (simulated 20 qps burst). we'll provide scripts and compute profiles.
05:30 Priya: for human eval we'll do pairwise comparisons? and what's your recommended evaluation metric?
05:36 Samir: pairwise A/B plus a graded pass/fail rubric for correctness/relevance. we typically use a 0-2 scale and compute pass-rate. will include template.
05:45 Maria: timeline — how quickly can we run this?
05:48 Alex: target: share shortlist & bench plan by 6/7, datasets by 6/9, pilot kickoff week of 6/16, 2-week pilot finishing roughly 6/30.
06:00 Eric: that fits our internal timeline.
06:05 Tom: any legal requirements for egress logs or audit?
06:10 Lena: we support audit logs and integration with your SIEM. Redwood Private includes longer retention as an add-on. we'll attach security pack.
06:22 Priya: on domain adaptation — would you recommend finetuning or retrieval? we prefer no fine tuning for Poc due to time.
06:30 Samir: recommended approach: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) + prompt engineering first; if quality isn't enough, small LoRA style fine-tune for top model after PoC. we'll test RAG vs base model outputs in the bench.
06:45 Maria: specific benchmarks for multilingual: please ensure we include native spanish prompts and some code-switching.
06:52 Samir: noted. we'll include code-switch cases and a domain-specific faq set.
07:00 Alex: any competitor avoidance or reasons zenoria picked redwood?
07:05 Maria: we liked the production-first approach, transparent perf profiles, and routing controls. also the ability to run in our VPC/KMS was important.
07:14 Priya: quick nit, could you include an example quantization profile numbers? like throughput tokens/s for 4-bit vs 8-bit?
07:21 Samir: yes, in the shortlist doc we'll include perf matrix: model x quant x instance type => p50/p95 and tokens/sec approx. expect big gains moving 70B from fp16 to 4-bit on supported kernels.
07:35 Alex: ok wrap up — recap and next steps?
07:40 Alex: we will send model shortlist + pros/cons, bench plan & scripts, security pack. zenoria will send datasets and confirm VPC requirements. target pilot kickoff week of 6/16.
07:55 Maria: thanks all. looking forward.
